address: Marnixstraat 248, Amsterdam (Marnixstraat car park): 1972 white concrete parking garage of six decks on an open pillared undercroft, round ramp towers
notes: Marnixstraat 248 (BAG: built 1972; one shop and one dwelling units; 3,241 m2 footprint, 22 m): the multi-storey car park on the Lijnbaansgracht / Marnixstraat corner with a petrol station in its undercroft. Three walls are photographed: the north-east front (w01-67, panorama 2023-03-06: a fuel-station canopy fascia with a red and white striped band under white decks), the south-east front (w03-157, 2022-06-28: six white concrete deck fronts, each a long ribbon of grey glass or louvre panels between white parapet bands with small slots, over an open undercroft carried on round pillars) and the south-west canal front (w02-247, 2021-01-25: the same decks wrapping the round ramp towers over the water).

Modelled: three ribbon-window groups (NE panels 179, 182, 204, 202; SE panels 160, 186; SW panels 63, 174, 59) as 7 storeys (a dark glazed undercroft and six deck ribbons), white wall colour, dark ribbon frames. Roofs are the 3DBAG LoD2.2 shell.

Simplified: the undercroft is a dark glazed ground row (the real one is open with round pillars, petrol pumps and a canopy), the ribbons are low windows cut into the white wall (the real deck fronts are glass or louvre panels set flush between parapet bands), the red/white striped fascia over the station is not drawn, the slot perforations in the parapet bands are not drawn, the round ramp towers keep the 3DBAG facets. Not modelled: the north-west side and the interior ramps (no useful view).

Refit 2026-10-25 (issue #59): the parking decks of w03-157 and w05 are continuous open ribbons between white parapet bands, broken only by thin columns, not windows punched bay by bay: windowShape w 0.97 (nearly the full bay), h 0.42 over a 0.4 parapet. walls[0]'s crop w01-67 is shot from under the petrol-station canopy: the dark undercroft and its lit soffit fill the frame, and the gate reads that shadow as a brick wall (#554a46) against the white render: a misread, allowed as inferred; walls[1] and walls[2] are washed out (55 %, 40 %).
